Date: 2027-05-16 17:00 UTC

Transcript body:
[00:00] Liam: Okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for making time. Uh, quick intro — I'm Liam Carter, AE at Redwood. With me is Maya, our SE — she'll drive the Optimize console demo.
[00:12] Evelyn: Hi, thanks. Evelyn here, CTO at BlueNova. We're excited, we— we ran your benchmark doc, looked promising.
[00:18] Rajesh: Hey this is Rajesh, ML eng. We mostly care about throughput at scale and not degrading the clinical fidelity of our answers — uh, for our internal risk scoring.
[00:25] Sofia: And Sofia, I run the data pipeline, I'll be owning the sample prompts and the dataset for the test.
[00:31] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: we'll show the Optimize console qprofile suggestions, spin up a sandbox run with INT8 and FP8 profiles, run a few prompts from BlueNova's sample set, look at latency/cost numbers, and then talk rollout strategies. Sound good?
[00:45] Evelyn: Yep.
[00:47] (screen share starts, slight audio lag)
[00:55] Maya: Alright I'm in the Optimize tab — first thing you'll see is the recommended qprofiles panel. For this model family we suggest two candidate profiles: an INT8-fast profile tuned for throughput and an FP8-balanced profile tuned for fidelity. The console shows expected token latency and a quality delta estimate based on our evals.
[01:20] Rajesh: Curious how you compute the quality delta — is that BLEU/Rouge-like or embedding-distance?
[01:26] Maya: Good question. It's a composite metric: we run your prompts through a holdout set and compute an embedding similarity score against gold answers plus a set of task-specific heuristics. It's not perfect but it flags likely regressions.
[01:40] (unintelligible mumble)
[01:48] Maya: I'm launching two sandbox runs now — INT8 profile on GPU pool A, FP8 on GPU pool B. Both pinned to the same model family and sequence length distribution.
[02:05] Liam: For cost context, INT8 run should show roughly 30-45% token-cost savings on our runtime vs FP16, FP8 is usually 10-20% savings but with smaller quality delta in many cases.
[02:20] Evelyn: Can you be specific — numbers our finance team will want.
[02:23] Liam: Sure — from similar customers we've seen median latency per token: INT8 ~45ms, FP8 ~70ms, FP16 ~120ms for that model at this sequence length distribution. Cost-per-token relative to FP16: INT8 ~0.55x, FP8 ~0.8x. But YMMV based on batch sizes and KV cache hit rate.
[02:50] Rajesh: That latency delta seems big — what about cold-start vs warmed kv-cache?
[02:55] Maya: Good catch — warm KV cache shaves about 20-30% off token latency in these runs. The console's latency projection assumes a steady-state with typical prefix reuse. We'll capture both cold/warm in the sandbox metrics.
[03:10] (console shows live logs and perf charts)
[03:25] Maya: Running the first prompt — patient-safety paraphrase from your test set. INT8 finished in 48ms tokens, FP8 in 72ms, FP16 in 118ms. Here's the output; INT8 made a minor truncation on a long tail chemical name, FP8 preserved it.
[03:50] Sofia: That truncation is concerning — in our domain a single token can flip a recommendation.
[03:55] Maya: Understood. That's exactly why we show the per-prompt similarity and a confidence delta. On the console you can drill into the exact token-level diffs and the top-k logits to see where quantization impacted token probabilities.
[04:15] Rajesh: Is there an automatic rollback if the quality delta exceeds our threshold in production?
[04:20] Liam: Yes — you can configure a rollout policy: start with 5% traffic on INT8, compare eval metrics against a gold set, and automatically revert to FP8/FP16 if the similarity drops more than X. We also recommend route-based pinning for critical endpoints.
[04:35] Evelyn: How intrusive is the switch? Our infra team wants minimal code changes.
[04:39] Maya: It's API-level: the model variant and qprofile are parameters in the same Redwood inference call. No app code change; you can mutate the route in the Console. For on-prem or Private deployments we also provide an operator tool for rolling profiles via config.
[04:58] (background typing)
[05:10] Maya: Back to the sandbox — here's the aggregated quality dashboard. FP8 retained 98.6% similarity to gold, INT8 95.1% on your set (small set, ~120 prompts). We flagged 7 low-confidence prompts for manual review, mostly long-tail token issues and numeric precision.
[05:36] Rajesh: On that small set — how confident are you that 95.1% isn't catastrophic at production scale?
[05:40] Maya: You can increase evaluation coverage, we recommend at least 1k prompts representing production traffic. Also use targeted stress tests for long sequences and numeric-heavy prompts. Our Optimize tool can generate adversarial prompts too.
[05:56] Liam: Also, hybrid strategies are common: INT8 for non-critical routes and FP8/FP16 for high-risk ones, or fallback on mismatched confidence.
[06:08] Sofia: What about the impact on throughput — if we batch aggressively does FP8 become better cost-wise?
[06:12] Maya: Batching helps all profiles, but INT8 often benefits more from high-concurrency kernels. The console shows a throughput vs latency heatmap so you can choose a sweet spot.
[06:25] (Maya toggles to canary rules)
[06:30] Maya: Here's a canary policy example: 5% traffic to INT8 for 48 hours, monitor embedding-similarity, error-rate, and tail latency. On breach, route 100% back to previous variant. You can hook alerts to PagerDuty and also log audit events to BigQuery/S3.
[06:52] Evelyn: On security — can the sandbox use VPC peering and our KMS for keys?
[06:56] Liam: For the Private offering yes; for hosted sandbox we can use customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) and set up a VPN or VPC peering for secure egress. We are SOC 2 certed and can share the security pack.
[07:12] Rajesh: How big a sample do you need to make an inference about quality delta? Is 120 prompts enough?
[07:18] Maya: Statistically no — but it surfaces obvious regressions quickly. We aim for a 1k-5k prompt benchmark for reliable estimates, stratified by route and token-length.
[07:30] (small crosstalk)
[07:40] Maya: Ok running a longer synthetic batch now — this will take ~6 minutes, we'll watch the distributions.
[07:50] (timestamps skip while batch runs)
[13:05] Maya: Results back — latency P50/P95: INT8 (P50 46ms, P95 122ms), FP8 (P50 69ms, P95 140ms), FP16 (P50 118ms, P95 210ms). Token-cost normalized: INT8 0.52x, FP8 0.81x vs FP16. Quality (embedding similarity mean): FP16 0.987, FP8 0.981, INT8 0.94 on this synthetic mix.
[13:35] Rajesh: P95 for INT8 is quite spiky — do you expose traces to see kernel fallback or out-of-memory induced slowdowns?
[13:41] Maya: Yes we've got per-request traces and you can filter for GC or kernel fallbacks. Some spikes correlate with outlier sequence lengths and off-host fetches. We also show GPU utilization timelines.
[13:55] Evelyn: Any guidance on how we tune qprofiles to get INT8 closer to FP8 quality?
[14:00] Maya: Two levers — targeted quant-calibration on problematic layers and mixed-precision profiles (e.g., keep embedding and norm layers in FP8 while quantizing attention matrices). Our Optimize console has a guided q-profile editor to make these changes and re-run quick checks.
[14:18] Liam: And we can provide a tuning engagement where our applied ML team runs a sensitivity sweep and produces recommended per-layer quant thresholds. That would be part of the pilot SOW if you'd like.
[14:30] Sofia: That sounds useful. How long would a sensitivity sweep take?
[14:33] Maya: With your dataset and a modest compute allocation, 3-5 days to run a decent sweep and summarize per-layer impact. Faster if you give us a smaller targeted set.
[14:45] Rajesh: One more — how do you handle deterministic outputs for auditing — quant noise may affect reproducibility.
[14:50] Maya: We support seed pinning and a reproducible mode that pins kernels and eliminates nondeterministic ops. It's slower but necessary for audits. Also all inference logs and inputs can be stored for later replay.
[15:02] (customer small discussion off mic)
[15:25] Liam: Quick customer question — any competitors that do this whole thing in-console?
[15:29] Evelyn: We've looked at a few.
[15:31] Liam: Right, Anthropic provides some quant docs, but they don't have the integrated qprofile bakeoff and automated rollback like Optimize. Lambda lets you self-host but fewer built-in per-route rollouts. Not a deep competitor callout, just context.
[15:50] Sofia: Ok practical — what's the pilot shape? We'll need sandbox access, a contract, and a short tuning engagement.
[15:57] Liam: Proposed pilot: 6-week pilot, weeks 1-2: sandbox onboarding and sample collection, week 3: sensitivity sweep, week 4: optimized qprofiles and smoke benchmarks, weeks 5-6: canary pilot on 10% traffic and final review. Pricing: see attached spreadsheet I'll send.
[16:18] Evelyn: Sounds reasonable, finance will need the numbers.
[16:22] Liam: I'll attach cost model with assumptions around token volumes and typical KV cache hit rates.
[16:28] Maya: Final note — console will export a qprofile artifact you can check into your repo; for Private deployments we can integrate into your CI to auto-apply.
[16:36] Rajesh: Good. Any red flags on infra from your side?
[16:39] Maya: Nothing unusual — just ensure the VPC peering rules allow the sandbox egress and give us the sample prompt set with anonymized PHI if present; we'll run in a restricted environment.
[16:52] Evelyn: OK we can anonymize.
[16:55] Liam: Alright, recap of next steps — Maya will send the console recording and qprofile export, I'll send pilot SOW and cost model, and Evelyn will share the 1k prompt sample and SLOs. We'll reconvene after initial smoke tests.
[17:12] Sofia: Thanks everyone.
[17:14] (meeting ends)
